name: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 with RMaxTS
one_liner: A Lean 4 prover is trained with proof-checker feedback, then searched with a tree search that rewards reaching new proof states.

loop.proposes: Lean 4 proofs and proof steps from a language model
loop.judged_by: The Lean 4 proof assistant, which accepts or rejects each proof and each step
loop.steers: Lean outcomes are the RL reward; at inference, RMaxTS tree search rewards new states to pick branches

headline_result: With RL plus RMaxTS at a sample budget of 32 x 6400 (mixture of two guiding prompts) it reaches 63.5% on miniF2F-test; on the ProofNet test set it reaches 25.3% at a budget of 4 x 6400. The paper calls both new state of the art at publication.
caveat: Numbers depend heavily on sample budget: the same model gets 50.0% to 54.9% at 32 to 3200 samples without search. The ProofNet validation set was used for expert iteration, so the test column is the clean one.
beyond_harness_note: Lean is the judge, its verdicts retrain the model weights, and a tree of many partial proofs is searched; the finished proof is checkable without the model.

sources.title: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5: Harnessing Proof Assistant Feedback for Reinforcement Learning and Monte-Carlo Tree Search

verification.notes: Read abstract and Tables 1 and 2 in the PDF text. 63.5% (miniF2F-test) and 25.3% (ProofNet test) are correct but the draft omitted conditions: 63.5% is RL + RMaxTS at 32 x 6400 samples with the mixture strategy; ProofNet 25.3% is 4 x 6400. Authors list starts Huajian Xin, DeepSeek.
